title: Filter by distance highlights deeper issues
body: The aspect of the filter distance being a feature locked behind a hefty paywall, due weekly, is certainly an issue well known by know, but it highlights certain aspects of this app that truly are concerning. First, it signals that its creators have little hope that they can garner enough users to populate an area, and thereby generate meaningful engagement to which their project can be deemed successful. Secondly, as a contingent of the first, they have since deemed that the app, which cannot generate enough local traffic, can be utilized to eek out the desire for which the app is envisioned (femdom, or female led relationships) and therefore can exploit a premium from those who have little recourse but to pay for a version that entitles them to a potential relationship at a distance less than 500 miles away. Exploitation is certainly nothing new in the dating app method, but as it pertains to this app, it seems unsustainable. This would ensue a method of pay that focuses users on large metropolitan areas(not unusual for dating apps) yet unusually, is wholly reliant on subscriptions from users who are increasingly isolated in rural settings, as they have little hope of finding anyone shy of 50 miles, unless they pay the premium. This would imply that the app can provide service only so long as they can profit off of users from rural or less populous city regions: a demographic that would largely shrink away , due to realizing they could find these relationships easier on other apps. TLDR the devs apparent lack of confidence in their app has led them to turn it into a pay pig system(ironic) that seeks to eek out cash from extreme isolated individuals(more so than normal dating apps) and will likely go belly up, once their shrinking number of paying users get fed up or realize they can move elsewhere. So please don’t waste your cash on it.

I emailed the support team and they replied pretty quickly, informing me that I was only 1 of 15 people to encounter this issue and that it was now fixed. They also gave me instructions on how to get my $3.99 back through Apple, albeit Apple has yet to refund me. They also told me I wasn’t supposed to see that screen, and I figured maybe the $3.99 a week would be for some premium experience after matching opened up or something, as many dating apps tend to do. Especially since it mentioned something about getting to the matches quicker (I don’t completely remember what exactly it said, so take that with a grain of salt.) Anyways, move forward in time a bit, and some regions haven’t been opened to matching yet (including mine) and I’m on a waiting list but they release global matching! Yippee!! Agree to global matching and find myself on… another waiting list. Sigh and move forward a little bit more. Finally, I have access to global matching. I open up the app, ready to start FINALLY using the app and encounter, once more, the pay wall. For real this time. And guess what? It’s NOT for a premium subscription or anything like that… it’s to USE THE APP!!! All this waiting and I finally give up and lose interest. $3.99 a WEEK for an app that’s barely out, and I don’t even get to use the free trial because it still thinks I’ve already subscribed due to the original error! So, long story short, I’ve lost faith in this app. Maybe if it were $3.99 a month I’d reconsider, but I don’t want to risk putting in money for an app I’m not sure will even be alive in a month, especially when my experience with the app has been lackluster and disappointing, and I haven’t even gotten to the main purpose of the app. I will say, the team of people running the app seem to be reasonable to work with, and according to their Instagram profile they work for free. Unfortunately, I didn’t exactly download the app with the intention of chatting with the staff team. So, please read this review and decide if this is all something you’re willing to put up with in an app. I’ve no doubt that Chyrpe will improve in the future, but right now it’s just not worth it, to me at least. Especially for $3.99 a week. And Chyrpe, at the very least make it clear when you first create an account that none of the primary features will be available unless you subscribe for $3.99 a week.
